features.title: Manage persistent agents
features.summary: Create, edit, enable and remove agents — handle, name, glyph, description, instructions, Agent preset, model route and reasoning effort — from one Host-owned registry every browser and agent reads. An agent keeps the threads it started (history and usage survive a Host restart), an optional routine line rides the opening message while the panel reads the reminders back from the Host's schedule catalog, and delegation targets constrain which Agents that agent's threads may message. A built-in @dsh agent ships with the harness defaults and cannot be deleted.
failureModes: A handle is a slug; a name alone is enough to create one.
Removing the built-in @dsh agent is refused and reported.
Removing an already-removed agent reports it as missing.
A save past the 100-agent limit is reported and existing agents stay.
A listed delegation refuses a peer it does not name, with a reason naming both handles.

features.title: Mention an agent where a thread starts
features.summary: A leading @handle dispatches an ordinary thread on that agent: its preset, its model route, its instructions and the user's text as the opening prompt. The @ menu lists enabled agents, @agent:/@a: narrows it, another source's scope stays empty, and a backlog comment box completes agent handles inline without hijacking @b:/@t:/@f:.
failureModes: An unknown handle stays a plain comment.
A disabled agent is not offered and does not dispatch.
A catalog without the agent's route leaves the Host default model.
